timeline_events.summary: Michelle Obama celebrated her 44th birthday at a campaign gathering in Nevada, where she delivered a speech advocating for her husband Barack Obama's presidential campaign.

Michelle Obama said at a Milwaukee rally that she had never really felt pride in America before her husband's campaign, drawing controversy and prompting Cindy McCain to express her own patriotism in response.
Michelle Obama says she wants to rip Bill Clinton's eyes out over his "fairytale" remark, then jokes "Kidding!"

Attention among rightwingers turns to Michelle Obama after her husband secures the Democratic presidential nomination, with Fox News anchor Ed Hill apologizing for describing her gesture as a "terrorist fist jab."

Fox News issued a quasi-apology after an onscreen caption referred to Michelle Obama as "Obama's Baby Mama," following a pundit's earlier description of the Michelle-Barack dap as a "terrorist fist jab."
Michelle Obama appears on The View to address and rebut criticisms, opening with a fist bump.
Michelle Obama appeared on ABC's The View amid media discussion of whether she needs a makeover.
Barack Obama said he regretted exposing his daughters to a mass television audience in their first family interview with Michelle Obama, saying it was not healthy and would be avoided in the future.

Media coverage of Michelle Obama during the 2008 presidential campaign included racist and sexist characterizations, such as a Fox News caption calling her "Obama's Baby Mama" and rightwing commentators labeling her an "angry black woman."
Michelle Obama gave her first major speech at the Democratic National Convention to present her family as typically American and humanize Barack Obama's presidential candidacy.

Michelle Obama delivered her first major speech at the Democratic National Convention, giving a personal account of her husband Barack Obama as a husband and father and praising Hillary Clinton's advancement of the women's movement.
Michelle Obama delivers a sunny, family-centric speech at the Democratic National Convention, a shift in tone from earlier remarks.
Michelle Obama acknowledged a good anniversary date at a fundraiser after celebrating her anniversary dinner with Barack Obama.
Michelle Obama campaigned for her husband Barack Obama in conservative Indiana, urging voters to support him in the November 4 election.
Michelle Obama wore a black and red Narciso Rodriguez dress on election night in Grant Park, Chicago, which drew widespread criticism.
Michelle Obama is preparing to move her family to Washington and is assembling a staff as she takes on the role of first lady.
Michelle Obama is preparing to become first lady, assembling a staff and planning her White House role while avoiding a policy role.
Cherie Blair advises Michelle Obama to learn to like the back seat.

Michelle Obama is described as being in a “domestication” role as she sets aside her professional views to be a grateful and gracious mom and wife, with the article noting she may later take a more substantive public role in policy making.
Bluewater Productions announces plans to feature Michelle Obama in the third book of its Female Force comic book series, scheduled for release in April 2009.
Michelle Obama had doubts about Rahm Emanuel being appointed White House chief of staff before moving into the White House in January 2009, according to a book.
Michelle Obama became first lady of the United States.
Michelle Obama focused on settling her daughters into school and unpacking at the White House during her first week as first lady.
Michelle Obama appeared on the cover of the March issue of US Vogue, with photographs by Annie Leibovitz.
Vogue confirmed that Michelle Obama would appear on its March cover and posted the text of Andre Leon Talley's interview along with a slideshow of the spread.
Michelle Obama appears on the cover of US Vogue, becoming only the second First Lady to do so.
Michelle Obama is reported to have significant influence on the fashion world, boosting relatively unknown designers such as Jason Wu after wearing his designs.

Jason Wu, a designer whose gown Michelle Obama wore to the Neighborhood Inaugural Ball, held a standing-room-only catwalk show for his autumn/winter collection at New York Fashion Week, amid heightened attention to Michelle Obama's fashion choices.
Barack Obama emails Michelle Obama suggesting they watch The Godfather: Part 4 in the White House cinema after work.
Michelle Obama is described as delegating fashion responsibilities to Chicago boutique owner Ikram Goldman, a claim reported by the New York Times.
Michelle Obama's picture appears on the cover of the March issue of US Vogue, not Vanity Fair.
Michelle Obama appeared on the cover of Vogue, becoming the first black woman to do so in America.
Oprah Winfrey shares the cover of O magazine with First Lady Michelle Obama for the first time, featuring an interview with her.
Michelle Obama and 26 Washington schoolchildren began digging a 1,100-square-foot organic kitchen garden on the White House South Lawn.

Michelle Obama met Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace during the G20 summit, wearing a regal black coat and presenting the Queen with an iPod loaded with video footage of her 2007 visit to Virginia.
Michelle Obama visited Elizabeth Garrett Anderson school in north London, where she addressed students and encouraged them to control their own destinies.
Michelle Obama joined Sarah Brown on a visit to Maggie's Cancer Caring Centre in west London, marking the centre's first anniversary.
Michelle Obama arrived in France for a two-day visit that included a meeting with Carla Bruni-Sarkozy.
Michelle Obama addressed 100 teenage girls at the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson school in north London, speaking about love, strong values, and a good education.
Michelle Obama hosted the annual White House Easter egg roll for 30,000 children and guests.
The White House released Barack and Michelle Obama's 2008 tax return, showing they made $2.7 million and donated $172,000 to charity.
Michelle Obama is described as refreshing the role of First Lady through her normal, educated, and professional persona, three months into the role.
Michelle Obama arrived in London with her daughters for a private, unofficial visit, touring Westminster and reportedly meeting Sarah Brown at Downing Street.
The White House admitted that Michelle Obama's vegetable garden tested positive for elevated lead levels, though below the EPA's danger threshold.
Michelle Obama spent the day at the Marriott hotel in Copenhagen where IOC members were staying to press home Chicago's message ahead of the vote on the 2016 Olympic Games.
Barack and Michelle Obama selected 45 artworks, including modern and contemporary pieces and works by Native American and black artists, to decorate the White House.

The New York Times, in conjunction with a professional genealogist, reveals that Michelle Obama's great-great-great-grandmother was a slave and her great-great-great-grandfather was a white man, reviving debate about the "one drop rule."
Michelle Obama harvests the White House garden.
A New York Times Magazine article reveals details of Barack and Michelle Obama's marriage, including past difficulties and their current family life in the White House.
Michelle Obama is to appear on Sesame Street to teach children how to grow a cucumber as the show celebrates its 40th anniversary.

Harvey and Paula Darden, a couple from Georgia who arrived a day early for a White House tour, were unexpectedly admitted to an invitation-only Veterans Day breakfast and met Barack and Michelle Obama.
Google refuses to remove an image depicting Michelle Obama with monkey features from its search results, instead purchasing an ad to explain its search results policy.

Article identifies Barack and Michelle Obama as icons of the decade, noting Michelle Obama's role in the 2008 campaign and her traditional first lady duties including planting a White House vegetable garden.
Michelle Obama launched the "Let's Move" campaign, a national initiative aiming to eliminate childhood obesity within a generation.
David and Samantha Cameron gave Michelle Obama scented candles from perfumier Miller Harris during the Obamas' state visit to the UK.
Michelle Obama backed Walmart's five-year plan to provide healthier and more affordable food options as part of her healthy eating initiative.
Tea Party figures Sarah Palin and Michele Bachmann criticize Michelle Obama's breastfeeding campaign, prompting a response from the first lady's office.
Michelle Obama announced she is writing a book about her White House vegetable garden, due in April 2012, with proceeds going to charity.
Michelle Obama visited Oxford University to meet with 37 schoolgirls from a north London school, encouraging them to apply to top universities.
Michelle Obama handed a baby to Barack Obama at a campaign event, after which the baby calmed down.
Michelle Obama and her daughters met Nelson Mandela in Johannesburg during their tour of southern Africa.
First Lady Michelle Obama and Jill Biden were booed at a Nascar rally in Miami-Dade, Florida.
Michelle Obama appeared on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, her first appearance since her husband took office, discussing life in the White House and her work with military families.
Michelle Obama invited One Direction to the White House Easter egg hunt, but the band declined due to a scheduled tour of Australia.
Michelle Obama's book "American Grown: The Story of the White House Kitchen Garden and Gardens Across America" is published.
Michelle Obama hails Disney Channel move to shun sugar-coated advertising.
Michelle Obama delivered a speech at the Democratic National Convention.
Michelle Obama and Ann Romney campaigned for female voters as a new poll showed Obama's lead among women had vanished, with the candidates tied at 47%.
Michelle Obama debuts a new 70s-style full fringe hairstyle ahead of the presidential inauguration.
Michelle Obama was heckled by Ellen Sturtz at a fundraiser and responded by confronting the heckler, saying "Listen to me, or you can take the mic but I'm leaving."
Michelle Obama unveils proposed rules for the most radical overhaul of US nutritional labels in 20 years as part of her Let's Move campaign.

Michelle Obama appeared as a guest star in the Parks and Recreation season finale, playing herself as the keynote speaker at the National Parks Conference and recruiting Leslie Knope to her Let's Move campaign.

Michelle Obama tweeted support for the #BringBackOurGirls campaign, posting a photo of herself holding a sign with the hashtag, amid global protests demanding the release of 257 kidnapped Nigerian schoolgirls.
Michelle Obama is to deliver the weekly radio address to draw attention to the kidnapped Nigerian schoolgirls.
Michelle Obama delivered the US president's weekly address to express outrage over the kidnapping of more than 300 Nigerian schoolgirls from Chibok.
Michelle Obama delivers her husband's weekly video address to express outrage over the kidnapping of more than 250 Nigerian schoolgirls by Boko Haram.
Michelle Obama delivered a tribute at Maya Angelou's memorial service, saying Angelou's words "carried a little black girl from the south side of Chicago all the way to the White House."
Michelle Obama became a guest curator for Upworthy, with her first blog post promoting her Reach Higher campaign to inspire American youth into further education.
Michelle Obama's guest list for the State of the Union viewing box includes individuals intended to highlight policy themes such as race and policing, the economy, and diplomacy.
Michelle Obama appeared at the State of the Union address wearing a gray Michael Kors suit.
Michelle Obama appeared on the Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon, discussing family, mom dancing, the White House Easter egg roll, and her healthy eating campaign.
Michelle Obama addressed graduates of Tuskegee University, speaking candidly about her experiences with racial and gender stereotypes as a Black woman in America.
Michelle Obama gave a commencement speech at Tuskegee University in which she discussed racial stereotypes and the experiences of women of colour.
Michelle Obama returns to London to promote her Let Girls Learn initiative, accompanied by her mother and daughters.
Michelle Obama is due to arrive in the UK to promote girls' education as part of her global campaign.
Michelle Obama is to meet Prince Harry and David Cameron on the first day of a two-day UK visit to promote her campaigns for girls' education and support for military families.
Michelle Obama spoke at an Apollo Theater event emphasizing the importance of educating girls.
Michelle Obama released her first rap video as part of her Reach Higher campaign to encourage kids to go to college.
The White House announces Michelle Obama's guest list for the State of the Union address, which includes an empty seat to represent victims of gun violence.
Michelle Obama wore a marigold Narciso Rodriguez dress with a purple coat to the State of the Union address.
Michelle Obama said at SXSW that she will not run for president.
Michelle Obama released a song titled "This is for My Girls" featuring Missy Elliott, Zendaya, and others to support her Let Girls Learn education initiative.
Michelle Obama hosted her final White House kitchen garden planting, inviting children who had participated in the first planting in 2009.
Michelle Obama delivered a commencement address attacking Donald Trump, warning graduates that intimidation and fear lead to national demise.
Melania Trump's Republican national convention speech appears to have lifted lines verbatim from a 2008 speech by Michelle Obama, though the Trump campaign denies the plagiarism accusations.
Michelle Obama appeared on James Corden's Carpool Karaoke, singing songs and discussing her Let Girls Learn initiative.
Michelle Obama delivered a speech at the Democratic National Convention, which was praised as her boldest yet.
Michelle Obama campaigned for Hillary Clinton at George Mason University, urging support for Clinton in the 2016 presidential election.
Michelle Obama hosted 2016 US summer Olympic and Paralympic teams at the White House, where she playfully used gymnast Simone Biles as an arm rest during a ceremony honoring the athletes.
Michelle Obama delivered a speech in New Hampshire denouncing Donald Trump over his sexually predatory behavior and treatment of women.
Michelle Obama and Hillary Clinton shared a stage in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, where Clinton praised Obama and Obama campaigned for Clinton's presidential bid.

Carl Paladino, co-chair of Donald Trump's New York presidential campaign, made racist comments about Michelle Obama in an interview, saying he would like her to "return to being a male and let loose in the outback of Zimbabwe" to live "in a cave with Maxie, the gorilla," and later denied the comments were racist.
Michelle Obama gave her final speech as first lady, urging young Americans to believe in the power of hope and vowing to make it her life's work to help disadvantaged children get to college.
Michelle Obama leaves the White House as her husband Barack Obama's presidency ends, with no plans to run for political office.
The Trump administration is discontinuing Michelle Obama's Let Girls Learn education program and scrapping certain health standards for school lunches tied to her healthy eating initiative.

Michelle Obama criticized the Trump administration for freezing regulations on school meal nutrition standards and delaying menu calorie labeling rules, speaking at a Partnership for a Healthier America summit in Washington.
Michelle Obama spoke about the racism she faced as first lady during an armchair conversation in Denver, Colorado.
Michelle Obama enters the gun control debate as senators announce a breakthrough deal.
Michelle Obama devotes weekly address to Nigerian girls.
Michelle Obama stated she was tired of being labeled as an "angry black woman," responding to allegations in a new book by Jodi Kantor that she was an "unrecognised force" within the White House.
Michelle Obama was among high-profile figures and celebrities who sparked protests around the world over the 2014 abduction of 276 girls from Chibok, Nigeria.
Michelle Obama called for the release of the abducted Chibok schoolgirls as part of the #BringBackOurGirls campaign.
Michelle Obama participated in the #BringBackOurGirls campaign following the 2014 kidnapping of Chibok schoolgirls by Boko Haram.

facts.text: On 2009-01-20, Michelle Obama became first lady of the United States.
On 2009-03-19, Michelle Obama and 26 Washington schoolchildren began digging a 1,100-square-foot organic kitchen garden on the White House South Lawn.
On 2009-07-02, the White House admitted that Michelle Obama's vegetable garden tested positive for elevated lead levels, though below the EPA's danger threshold.
On 2010-02-09, Michelle Obama launched the "Let's Move" campaign, a national initiative aiming to eliminate childhood obesity within a generation.
On 2012-09-04, Michelle Obama delivered a speech at the Democratic National Convention.
On 2014-05-07, Michelle Obama tweeted support for the #BringBackOurGirls campaign, posting a photo of herself holding a sign with the hashtag, amid protests over kidnapped Nigerian schoolgirls.
On 2016-07-21, Michelle Obama appeared on James Corden's Carpool Karaoke, singing songs and discussing her Let Girls Learn initiative.
